speaker: Doctor

Good morning, I can see you have several skin lesions. To help me understand your condition, could you tell me how long you've had them and if they have changed in appearance? Also, do you feel itchy or painful in those areas?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
REQUEST TEST: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR)

text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count (CBC): WBC 6,000 /μL, Hemoglobin 12 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR): NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is an interesting observation from your previous doctor, as those specific skin findings—skin-colored, nontender papules with central umbilication—are classic for Molluscum Contagiosum, not appendicitis. Let's verify the extent of the infection; could you tell me how many individual lesions you currently have visible?

REQUEST TEST: Rapid Molluscum Contagiosum PCR Swab (if available)
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of the lesions

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR): NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum

Based on your description of skin-colored, nontender papules with central umbilication, and confirmed by the normal ESR results which rule out significant systemic inflammation, this clinical picture is classic for Molluscum Contagiosum. The previous suggestion of appendicitis was incorrect given these specific dermatological findings. Do you have any history of close contact with other individuals or attendance at swimming pools recently?
